day.reading: G_f is a measured throughput that already includes parallel fixation (G1 q1)
day.holds: on that reading T/G_f is the aggregate form and no parallelism factor is owed; the identity shows such a G_f is shorter than the per-allele time when sweeps overlap

critic.reading: dividing a window by a per-allele time assumes each fixation ends before the next starts
critic.holds: the two forms coincide only with no overlap; the critique holds against the Appendix A 'fixation must be sequential' chain (G2g), which Day's para 25 concedes is not purely serial

notes: Structural, exact on rationals. Over a window, G_f equals the start spacing; the serial and aggregate counts coincide only when it equals t_fix (back to back). Overlap makes the aggregate count larger by the mean concurrency, gaps make it smaller. p^n depends on (p, n) only (M-703), so neither reading changes it. The sources differ in target: Hancock (GG-01), Ghijselen (DZ-01), Camestros (CA-05), Myers (PZ-01, PZ-05) and Bowers (BO-02) are scored against the Appendix A chain or the 'generations per fixation' wording, not against T/G_f read as a throughput. The 66,000 and 20,000 divisions (Z23003785 s8.2) are drift fixation times, so those two are serial readings in Day's own text.
